title: The Vocative
subtitle: Direct address — calling someone by name.
objectives: Understand the vocative as the case of direct address.
Form the vocative for first- and second-declension nouns.
Recognize the particle ὦ as the marker of vocative address.
Distinguish the vocative from the nominative where the forms differ.

sections.heading: The vocative case
sections.body:
The vocative is the case you use when addressing someone directly. ὦ Σώκρατες means 'O Socrates' or 'Hey, Socrates.' The particle ὦ is often used with the vocative, but it is not required.

In many nouns, the vocative is identical to the nominative. In the second-declension masculine, the vocative singular is distinct: -ε instead of -ος. In the first-declension masculine, the vocative singular is also distinct: -ᾰ (short α) instead of -ης or -ας.

The vocative never takes an article. You do not say ὁ Σώκρατες in the vocative; you just say Σώκρατες or ὦ Σώκρατες.

sections.heading: Vocative forms
sections.body:
Second-declension masculine:
  nominative  ὁ ἄνθρωπος
  vocative    ὦ ἄνθρωπε

First-declension masculine:
  nominative  ὁ ποιητής
  vocative    ὦ ποιητά

First-declension feminine in -η:
  nominative  ἡ ἀρετή
  vocative    ὦ ἀρετή (same as nominative)

Second-declension neuter:
  nominative  τὸ τέκνον
  vocative    ὦ τέκνον (same as nominative)

The vocative plural is always identical to the nominative plural in all declensions.

sections.heading: Examples from Plato
sections.body:
Plato, Crito 43a: ὦ Σώκρατες.
'O Socrates.' The vocative form of Σωκράτης is Σώκρατες (drop the -ης, leave the stem).

Plato, Apology 17a: ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι.
'O men of Athens.' ἄνδρες is the vocative plural of ἀνήρ (man); Ἀθηναῖοι is the vocative plural of Ἀθηναῖος (Athenian). Both are identical to the nominative plural.

items.answer: Direct address — calling out to someone.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 2.10 introduces the verb εἰμί (to be), the most common verb in Greek. The present indicative forms are irregular but essential. εἰμί, εἶ, ἐστί, ἐσμέν, ἐστέ, εἰσί. Once you know εἰμί, you can form predicate sentences and express existence.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can form the vocative singular and plural of any first- or second-declension noun and can recognize the vocative in Greek sentences.
